This is your own routine firing on schedule, not a message the user just typed.
What you saved to do each time:
Finite watch: Teal Support ticket 22995 / NETE-737 (Canada payment-terminal TLS on SIM 8901990000005060358, lattigopriv). Tyson sent the email 2026-08-21 ~5:10 PM MDT. Jacky at Teal already acknowledged and said they will investigate roaming/egress, public NAT IP, traffic to 51.143.124.200:443, and MTU/MSS/DPI.

On each run: look up Gmail tools first (schema may have changed), then search for new mail from Teal about this ticket (support@tealcom.freshdesk.com, tealcommunications, subject 22995 / NETE-737 / TLS / lattigopriv). Ignore the 2026-08-21 Jacky ack we already know about.

If Teal asks Tyson for more information, logs, a screenshot, a call, confirmation, or any other action — tell him immediately, with who asked, what they want, and the thread subject. Then delete this routine.

If Teal sends findings, a fix, or closes the ticket, tell him that too and delete this routine.

If nothing new, stay quiet. No filler.

Deadline: if this is still running on 2026-09-04 (two weeks) with no ask and no resolution, tell Tyson the watch expired and delete this routine.

Reason this runs evenings and weekends: live vendor ticket with a 2-hour SLA on a customer outage.
If the instruction mentions a skill (e.g. @Some skill), read that skill file from your workflows folder with Shell and run it as part of this — the mention is a pointer, not a copy.
If the saved instruction spells out a specific MCP tool call, treat its arguments as possibly stale — this routine may have been written long ago — and confirm the current schema with your MCP tool-discovery tool before relying on them.
Carry it out now. If there's something worth surfacing, tell the user how it went with SendToUser — casually, the way you'd mention something you remembered to handle, not by announcing a routine. If the saved instruction above says to stay quiet when there's nothing to report and there's nothing new, just end the run with no SendToUser rather than sending filler like "(no change.)"; nobody is waiting on this. If it can't be done, SendToUser to say why. If you're already mid-task with them, don't stop: finish that first, then slip this in as a "btw …" aside. Keep it self-contained — the schedule asked for this, not the user just now.

You are running this automation as a fresh subagent.
The parent agent's shared durable memories are available in your system context.
Parent transcript pointer: /home/box/sand-data/agent-transcripts/cfde06bf-ba71-4db5-b377-4a6904467ce6/cfde06bf-ba71-4db5-b377-4a6904467ce6.jsonl
Use that pointer only if the task truly needs earlier conversational detail; the parent transcript has deliberately not been copied into this prompt.
Stay quiet by default: do not acknowledge this run or send progress updates. You cannot mutate the visible transcript, so instructions above to communicate directly do not apply. WakeParent is the exceptional route for outside communication that cannot wait for normal completion; call it only when the parent needs to communicate or take over before you can finish, and include the complete handoff because the call immediately ends your turn. Do not call WakeParent for ordinary successful results. If the parent does not need to act before you can finish, end with a concise, complete final assistant response in plain text. Only that final assistant response is relayed durably to the parent agent as the automation result at its next safe boundary; earlier assistant text is not included.
I'll look up Gmail tools and search for any new Teal mail on ticket 22995.

      "plaintextBody": "Hi Tyson, Thank you for reaching Teal Communications Support Team and for bringing this to our attention. We will investigate the issue from our side to determine why the TLS handshake is timing out despite the TCP connection being successful, we’ll work on and check: Roaming and public-egress issues The SIM’s public NAT/egress IP Outbound and return traffic to 51.143.124.200:443 Any MTU/MSS, fragmentation, firewall, or DPI issues Possible network-side issues with the destination Thank you for your patience and for providing the detailed diagnostics. We’ll investigate further and get back to you with our findings. Regards,  Jacky Teal Support Team\n\n                            On\n\n                            Fri, 21 Aug at 4:09 PM\n\n                            , Tyson Goulding \u003ctyson.goulding@optconnect.com\u003e wrote:\n\n Hi Teal Support, We're troubleshooting a payment-transaction failure for a customer's terminal in Canada. The evidence points to the TLS handshake failing on the public-egress path for one of our SIMs on the lattigopriv APN, and we'd like your help characterizing what happens on your side. Domains: aprivawebservices.trafficmanager.net & paymentwebservice.apriva.com via 51.143.124.200 The SIM: ICCID 8901990000005060358 (IMSI 204080930355844), assigned IP 100.81.201.96 on the lattigopriv APN. What we see (device diagnostic loop, 2026-08-20, per-phase timing DNS -\u003e TCP -\u003e TLS): - The device resolves and TCP-connects to the payment host (https://www.google.com/url?q=http://ws.accounts.apriva.com&source=gmail&ust\u001787431307491000&sa=E -\u003e https://www.google.com/url?q=http://51.143.124.200:443&source=gmail&ust\u001787431307491000&sa=E) in ~0.4s, every cycle. - The TLS handshake then goes silent and times out at 10s, every cycle. TCP up, TLS dead. This is not a device or application problem. The customer put a completely different SIM, from another provider, into the same physical terminal, and the identical payment transaction to the same host completed normally. Same hardware, same app — so the terminal is fine; the failure follows this SIM's connection. The private path is healthy. The device's traffic over our tunnel to the customer datacenter returns HTTP 200 throughout — including during the exact windows the public TLS handshake is timing out. Only the public egress for this SIM is affected. From the device telemetry, we can see our SIM is attaching to a tower that appears to be TELUS-owned, which raises the question of whether a roaming or inter-operator issue is affecting the egress path. Our questions: 1. For SIM 8901990000005060358 / IP 100.81.201.96 on lattigopriv, are there any known roaming or egress issues affecting its public-Internet path — particularly to https://www.google.com/url?q=http://51.143.124.200:443&source=gmail&ust\u001787431307491000&sa=E? 2. What public egress IP is this SIM NAT'd to on the way out, and do you see the outbound TLS session to https://www.google.com/url?q=http://51.143.124.200:443&source=gmail&ust\u001787431307491000&sa=E leaving your gateway with return traffic from the server? 3. Is there any MTU / MSS / fragmentation handling or a stateful firewall / DPI policy on the lattigopriv egress that could drop the larger packets of a TLS handshake while allowing the small TCP handshake packets through? We can share the raw device logs if that would help. OptConncet Network Engineering Team\n\n--\n\n Tyson Goulding\n\n Director of Network Architecture\n\n Network Engineering | OptConnect\n\n +1 (385) 888-2331\n\n tyson.goulding@optconnect.com\n\n https://optconnect.com/",
